name: Touch the surface grinder's wheel off on the work: down until it just sparks, the down-feed dial zeroed; and its side off on an edge, by the cross-feed dial

working.role: turns the down-feed handwheel and sets its dial; turns the cross-feed handwheel

steadying.role: rocks the table by its handwheel to bring the work under the wheel and away again

phases.what: With the wheel running and the coolant off, the table traversed and the saddle fed to bring the work just beside the wheel, the head lowered fast by the down-feed handwheel to a few millimetres above the work [proposed: force_n, duration_s, the gap]
phases.ends_on: the wheel's bottom about 1 mm above the work, by eye

phases.what: Then a graduation (0.0002 in) at a time, the table rocked a little under the wheel between each, until a first spark [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: a single spark, or a faint scratch on the work

phases.what: Hold the handwheel and turn the dial alone to its zero: that is the work's top [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the dial at zero, the handwheel unmoved

phases.what: For a slot set from an edge: raise the wheel clear, bring its side to the edge with the cross-feed until it just sparks on the edge, note the cross dial, raise clear again, and feed across by the dial to where the slot begins [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the cross dial at the slot's offset from the edge

sources.ref: South Bend Lathe Co., Model SB1029 Owner's Manual (2010): Operation Overview (p. 20, step 5: the wheel lowered to just above the work's top), Using the Surface Grinder (p. 32: the elevation handwheel governs the stock removed; the cross handwheel between passes), Machine Specifications (vertical handwheel 0.0002 in a graduation, 0.05 in a turn; cross 0.001 in, 0.2 in)
sources.gives: the wheel down to just above the work; the handwheels' graduations

sources.ref: The station's down-feed and its friction-held dial (moonshot/library/stations/sgrind.json joints.downfeed_handwheel, downfeed_dial; its gate test_sgrind_conformance.py), and the ct-tpg322 plan's datum (the wheel touched down on the insert's top and the dial zeroed)
sources.gives: a graduation at a time to the touch; the dial turned alone to zero without moving the wheel

sources.ref: The ct-tpg322 plan's cross datum: the wheel's outer side set .010 in inside the cutting edge with the cross-feed, by the dial from the wheel's side touched on the edge (moonshot/planning/plans/ct-tpg322.json setups op10 datum.cross)
sources.gives: the side touch-off on an edge and the offset by the cross dial

notes: On this grinder the down-feed handwheel is on the column's right side, 1.4 m up, and the table and cross handwheels are at the front: a hand on the down-feed can't reach the table's, so a touch-off made from the down-feed's side brings the work under the wheel first and lowers onto it there, and the plan's hand grind splits each pass into a front take and a right-side take (your decision, 2026-11-06). The steadying hand's rocking applies where both are in reach. A spark is the touch: the dial's zero is the part's top within a graduation. No footage of a touch-off is measured yet. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): #1 8 N at the knob (the station's down-feed takes about 1 N m) and 5-15 s, the gap of about 1 mm by eye; #2 4 N and 10-30 s, a graduation at a time over the last 1 mm being up to 200 of them, most taken a few at a time until close; #3 2 N on the dial (its friction 0.4 N m at 100 mm) and 1.5 s; #4 3 N on the cross knob and 10-25 s for the side touch and the offset.
